description: In this team, We will present a work of fiction based on abandoned NASA equipment discarded on the surfaces of the Moon and Mars after having fulfilled their tasks and acquired the necessary data.
summary:
'Abandoned But Not Forgotten: The Lost Hardware Archive' is an interactive educational game set in the future, and explores the history of man-made equipment left behind in space. Developed as a digital space archaeology experience, it allows young players to become space enthusiasts and archaeologists, investigate different missions and outcome that took place years before, recover the artefacts left behind, and completely rebuild the incomplete archive.

The project addresses the challenge by bringing attention to spacecraft, instruments, and hardware that remain on the Moon, Mars, and throughout the Solar System after their missions end. Through exploration, visual storytelling and artefact records, players learn about the significance and history of these objects.

The project is important because abandoned space hardware is often overlooked despite their scientific and practical value. Presenting these forgotten gems as stories in an engaging, interactive way will capture the attention of young curious minds towards space and raise awareness of humanity's last presence beyond our Earth, and demonstrates that the end of a mission does not mean the end of its story.
details:
Project DetailsAbandoned but Not Forgotten: Lost Hardware Archive

1. What does the project do, and how does it work?

Abandoned but Not Forgotten: Lost Hardware Archive is an interactive educational game that introduces players to space archaeology and the history of human-made equipment left behind during space exploration.

Players take on the role of a young space archaeologist assigned to reconstruct an incomplete digital archive. They explore different mission sectors, investigate abandoned hardware, recover digital artefacts, and unlock information about the objects they discover. Each artefact provides details about its original purpose, associated mission, location, and historical significance.

The game includes an introductory storyline, interactive mission environments, artefact-recovery sequences, a collection gallery, mission-completion screens, and a concluding narrative called The Last Transmission.

2. What benefits does it have?

The project makes the history of space exploration more accessible and engaging, particularly for students and young audiences. Instead of presenting information through conventional articles or static presentations, it encourages players to discover information through exploration.

Its benefits include:

  • Introducing players to the concept of space archaeology.
  • Increasing awareness of equipment left on the Moon, Mars, and in deep space.
  • Encouraging independent exploration and curiosity about science and technology.
  • Helping players understand the historical significance of completed space missions.
  • Presenting scientific and historical information through interactive storytelling.

3. What is the intended impact?

The intended impact is to change how people perceive abandoned space equipment. Objects left behind after a mission are not simply forgotten machines; they represent technological achievements, scientific discoveries, and important chapters in human history.

The project aims to encourage greater appreciation of humanity's presence beyond Earth and raise awareness of the historical and scientific value of space hardware. It also hopes to inspire younger audiences to explore careers and interests in astronomy, engineering, planetary science, and space exploration.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software were used?

The game was developed as a browser-based digital experience using:

  • HTML5: Provides the structure and organization of the game.
  • CSS3: Controls the visual design, layouts, typography, colors, and interface styling.
  • JavaScript: Handles gameplay logic, interactions, mission progression, artefact recovery, and game transitions.
  • HTML Canvas: Supports the graphical and interactive game environment.
  • AI-assisted image generation: Used to help create illustrative visual assets.
  • AI-assisted coding: Used during development and refinement of the game.

The project is designed to run in a modern web browser on a computer. No specialised hardware is required.

5. How is the project creative?

The project's central creative idea is to combine space archaeology with interactive storytelling. Space hardware is usually discussed in terms of its engineering or scientific purpose, but this game approaches it as historical evidence waiting to be rediscovered.

Players do not simply read about abandoned equipment; they become investigators who recover artefacts and gradually reconstruct an incomplete archive. The storyline, mission-based progression, visual exploration, recovery system, and final transmission create a sense of discovery.

The project also transforms a complex scientific subject into an accessible experience without losing sight of its historical significance.

6. What factors were considered during development?

Several factors guided the development process:

  • Historical relevance: The game focuses on real space missions and equipment, with an emphasis on communicating their historical context accurately.
  • Educational value: Information is presented in a way that encourages learning through exploration.
  • Accessibility: The browser-based format allows players to access the game without specialized equipment.
  • User experience: Clear instructions, readable text, recognizable mission sectors, and consistent navigation help players understand the gameplay.
  • Visual communication: Space-themed environments and illustrative artefacts help create an engaging atmosphere.
  • Technical functionality: Mission progression, recovery records, archive completion, and the ending sequence were considered when designing the game.
  • Responsible use of AI and visual assets: AI-assisted image generation and coding are acknowledged, and visual assets should be reviewed for appropriate attribution and compliance with the challenge rules.

Conclusion

Abandoned but Not Forgotten: Lost Hardware Archive brings together science, history, technology, and storytelling to explore an often-overlooked part of space exploration. By allowing players to investigate and recover the stories behind abandoned space hardware, the project communicates a simple idea: the end of a mission does not mean the end of its historical value.
